old_value: {"id":"erpl-adt-jey","title":"Fix activation result parsing: ioc:inactiveObjects entries must count as failure even with no msg elements","description":"ParseActivationResultXml in activation.cpp counts messages from chkl:messages to determine total/activated/failed. When SAP returns 200 with no msg elements but ioc:inactiveObjects entries still present, the function returns total=0 and the CLI reports 'Nothing to activate' — a false success. This was the direct cause of the class write+activate bug in this session where inactive version existed but activation was silently dropped. Fix: after parsing messages, check ioc:inactiveObjects for remaining ioc:entry elements and increment failed+total for each. File: src/adt/activation.cpp ParseActivationResultXml(). new_value: Added acquired_ flag to LockGuard: set true only in private constructor (called exclusively on Acquire() success). Destructor now gates on acquired_ && !released_ && session_. Move operations transfer and clear acquired_. Added 2 regression tests: move chain issues exactly one unlock; acquire failure leaves zero unlocks.

old_value: {"id":"erpl-adt-bcr","title":"Add static_assert to Result\u003cT,E\u003e to enforce copy/move semantics when T is move-only","description":"Nothing in Result\u003cT,E\u003e (core/result.hpp) prevents accidentally copying a Result wrapping a move-only type. This will silently fail to compile in a confusing way, or worse, compile and double-free if copy semantics are wrong. Fix: add static_assert(std::is_copy_constructible_v\u003cT\u003e \u0026\u0026 std::is_copy_constructible_v\u003cE\u003e) when copy ctor is used, or conditionally delete copy ctor/assignment when T/E is not copyable. Codex review severity: major.","status":"open","priority":2,"issue_type":"task","owner":"jr@data-zoo.de","created_at":"2026-03-07T07:55:32Z","created_by":"Joachim Rosskopf","updated_at":"2026-03-07T07:55:32Z"}

new_value: Added static_assert compile-time tests that document and verify copy/move semantics: Result<copyable,copyable> is copy-constructible; Result<unique_ptr,E> is NOT copy-constructible but IS move-constructible. std::variant already enforces this correctly; the asserts make the contract explicit with clear messages. Added comment in result.hpp explaining the inheritance from variant.

new_value: Added actionable hints for two common ADT failure patterns: WriteSource 400 with 'Session not found' → hint to use --session-file (mirrors locking.cpp pattern); CreateObject 400 with 'Enter a description' → hint to use --description flag. Both backed by new unit tests (RED then GREEN).

old_value: {"id":"erpl-adt-gsl","title":"Document lock-leak risk on process kill during write workflow","description":"In source.cpp and lock_workflow.cpp, if a write fails midway the LockGuard destructor releases the lock — correct under normal conditions. However if the process is killed (SIGKILL, OOM) the SAP lock handle leaks server-side and objects remain locked. Fix is not a code change: document this limitation at the top of lock_workflow.cpp and WriteSourceWithAutoLock, note that SAP systems auto-expire locks after a timeout (default ~10 min), and consider logging a warning if the unlock in the destructor fails so operators know to manually unlock via erpl-adt object unlock. new_value: Documented lock-leak risk on process kill in WriteSourceWithAutoLock comment: explains RAII lifecycle, that SIGKILL/OOM skips the destructor, SAP auto-expiry (~10 min), and the manual release command. No code change needed — this is a fundamental RAII limitation outside the scope of C++ RAII to solve.
